ai_technology: AlphaFold 3; structural comparison supported by molecular dynamics

evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold3-based domain comparisons predicted a local linker conformational difference that motivated targeted functional substitution tests. Conventional experiments, not the structural model alone, established the measured activity changes.
evidence.tested: Biochemical reconstitution, native-host genetic tests and substrate profiling supported distinct condensation-domain functions. Structural-model-guided linker substitutions restored detectable product in a disabled-domain background; full-linker rescue was approximately 0.25% of the reference.
evidence.unknown: Modelled conformations are predictions; experiments support a bounded linker contribution, not a complete molecular mechanism or broad generality across peptide synthetases. The small restoration does not establish an efficient production platform or therapeutic benefit.

organization: Shenzhen Bay Laboratory; The University of Hong Kong; Peking University

source_review.scope: Primary 30-page preprint PDF relevant structural-modelling Methods, Results linking predicted linker difference to functional tests, limitations and posted-date stamp; no supplement audit.

summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint reports that structural predictions helped identify a linker associated with repeated chain extension by the nonribosomal peptide synthetase DidA. AlphaFold-guided comparisons led to targeted experiments supporting a role for the linker in the different activities of two condensation domains. Transferred linker regions restored detectable peptide production in a disabled-domain background, but rescue was small relative to the reference and the work does not establish broad portability across synthetases.
title: Model-guided experiments identify a linker role in iterative peptide assembly
